Subject: Shoreline / Redwood: plugfest kickoff & artifacts

Thanks again for hosting the plugfest this morning — great to get Shoreline's team, QA, and our infra folks in the same room. Attaching the test matrix we ran and the reference design we used for the session. High-level notes below; full test matrix attached as plugfest-test-matrix.csv.

Quick summary: 
- Total scenarios executed: 48 (see matrix)
- Passing: 36; Partial: 7; Failing: 5
- Top failure buckets: auth token exchange (intermittent), KV cache eviction divergence, and one quantized kernel mismatch on T4-based nodes.

Immediate asks: 
1) Shoreline: can you share the raw QA traces for the three auth failures (qa@shoreline.ai) — referenced in row groups E3/E4 in the matrix?
2) Redwood: we’ll produce a short patch for the KV cache (probable race when prefix cache TTL > 60s) and post a test build by tomorrow EOD.

Attachments: redwood-shoreline-reference-design-v1.pdf (reference), plugfest-test-matrix.csv (results)

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Partner Integrations — Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com

From: Anika Bose <anika@shoreline.ai>

Subject: Re: Shoreline / Redwood: plugfest kickoff & artifacts

Alex — thanks for the summary and the matrix. We pulled the traces for the auth failures and uploaded a zipped bundle (error-sample-traces.zip) to the shared folder (link in the matrix). Quick findings from QA: 

- Auth token exchange: 3 intermittent 401s tied to a race in token refresh when concurrent ephemeral keys are requested. We can reproduce in our staging with 20 concurrent requests.
- KV cache divergence: we observed cases where the TTL skew caused stale prefixes to be served for ~35s after a rollover; looks like a locking window mismatch between Redwood's in-node cache and our edge proxy.
- Quantized kernel mismatch: failing scenario only on T4 with driver 470.x — NVIDIA updated a microcode path that changes fp16 conv rounding. Other machines (A100, V100) are fine.

We validated 36 of the scenarios as green. We've attached shorelines internal CSV for the raw runs and included row-level remarks in column 'qa_notes'.

Next steps we propose from Shoreline: 
1) We'll retest auth refresh with a patched token client (we can deploy a feature-flagged build tomorrow).
2) Our ops can stand up a T4 node with driver 465.x for compatibility testing if Redwood recommends that as a temporary mitigation.

Thanks,
Anika Bose
Head of Integrations — Shoreline.ai
anika@shoreline.ai

----

Subject: Re: Shoreline / Redwood: plugfest kickoff & artifacts — token race plan

Following up with a short technical plan for the auth token race and the KV cache mitigation. TL;DR: small code change + a defensive mutex per key + stronger metrics.

Plan — auth token race (PR referenced above):
- Root cause: concurrent refresh requests can call the token provider twice when TTL < 10s; second write overwrites the cached token while the first response is still being processed.
- Fix: add an in-process singleflight-style mutex keyed by refresh_id; first caller triggers refresh, others wait on the result; fallback path retains last-known-good until new token validated.
- Tests: unit tests + a small stress harness that simulates 50 concurrent refreshes.
- Rollout: feature flag on token client, can flip per-customer.

KV cache mitigation:
- Short-term: increase overlap grace window from 5s -> 45s and emit TTL-drift metrics to Datadog.
- Long-term: centralize eviction coordination via a lightweight distributed lock using existing Redis lock namespace.

Request for Shoreline: can you run the auth stress harness against your staging gateway once the PR is ready? Anika, if you give us a slot tomorrow morning we’ll push the flagged build.

Karthik
Staff Software Engineer — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Anika / Darren — thanks for the quick validation and the traces. We reviewed Karthik’s PR and Marissa’s KV mitigations; after the fixes and a short retest we’re comfortable moving to a soft MVP for the joint connector. Outstanding items before full partner listing: 

1) Shoreline to run the auth stress harness against your staging gateway after we publish the flagged build (Karthik) — target window: Wed 25 Aug 09:00–11:00 PT.
2) We will provide temporary guidance to prefer driver 465.x on T4 hosts for partner runs; ops teams to sync on any cost impact.
3) Both teams to confirm post-rollout observability: three synthetic checks (token exchange, prefix TTL, kernel-compat) pass for 48 hours.

If the above items pass, Redwood will greenlight the partner connector MVP and publish the reference design as an integration recipe (we’ll link the published doc in the shared drive). Proposed follow-up: 30-minute sign-off call Thu 26 Aug 10:00 PT.

Thanks again — great collaboration.

Alex Martinez
